title: GPT-4 stratifies post-discharge suicide risk from narrative discharge summaries
summary: In a matched case-control cohort of 11,970 patients from two academic medical centers (1995 deaths by suicide or accident, 5 matched controls each), gpt-4-1106-preview estimated risk from discharge summaries. Time to 90% survival was 1588 days in the lowest-risk quartile and 302 days in the top quartile; the adjusted hazard ratio was 8.86 (95% CI 7.00-11.2). Estimated risks were higher for Black and Hispanic individuals, and the study is retrospective, so clinical use and fairness remain open.
ai_technology: GPT-4 (gpt-4-1106-preview) estimating suicide risk from narrative discharge summaries

evidence.tested: Retrospective matched case-control analysis with linked vital-status data.
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance, calibration and the cause of racial and ethnic score differences; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A large language model estimated risk from clinical notes.
